newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia, Thailand agree to expand economic ties.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia, Thailand agree to expand economic ties.

text.p: Indonesia's President Suharto and Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh agreed on Friday to expand economic cooperation and increase consultations between their nations, Indonesia's State Secretary Murdiono said. The two leaders met at the state palace in central Jakarta before Chavalit left for home after midday at the end of a two-day official visit, his first trip abroad since taking office in November.
"President Suharto explained developments in Indonesia and the prime minister outlined the situation in Thailand," Murdiono told reporters after their 90-minute meeting.
"Both leaders saw the opportunity for expanding economic cooperation. They also agreed on the importance of increased consultations, if necessary by telephone," he added.

They agreed to work on a memorandum of understanding covering trade between the two countries and fisheries. Murdiono said they also stressed the importance of bilateral exchanges between officials and businessmen.
In a speech at a banquet he hosted for Chavalit on Thursday, Suharto called for closer cooperation between Indonesia and Thailand in the economic field, trade and technology.

Suharto said Indonesia -- by far the most populous country in Southeast Asia with some 200 million people -- was closely watching Thailand's efforts to become a centre for trade, investment, finance and tourism in the region.
"In this respect, both countries need to improve their cooperation, especially economic, trade and technical cooperation," Suharto said.
Murdiono said the two leaders had agreed during Friday's talks that no major problems existed between Indonesia and Thailand.

He said that in separate talks between Thai Foreign Minister Prachuab Chaiyasarn and Indonesia's Ali Alatas, Prachuab had expressed appreciation for Jakarta's willingness to supply Thailand from the huge Natuna natural gas field when it is developed in the South China Sea.
Indonesia's state oil company Pertamina said it was still negotiating with Thailand over Natuna gas supplies through an underwater pipeline.
Murdiono said the ministers had agreed Indonesia would open a consulate in southern Thailand, while Bangkok would open a consulate in Indonesia's second city of Surabaya in East Java.

Chavalit arrived in Jakarta on Thursday for what diplomats said was primarily a courtesy visit, following a custom of new leaders of member-nations of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) to call first on fellow ASEAN states.
ASEAN comprises Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam.
